ActionOutputId.description:
The stable identity one subscription follows (RFC 001 8.1).

The incarnation is service-issued when the action entity is
created; inspection returns it and the compiler verifies it, so
deleting and recreating an action does not attach old subscribers
to a new calculation.
ActionOutputId.title: ActionOutputId

ArtifactRecord.description:
One immutable artifact as the service verified it (section 5.1).

The record carries every verified fact of the registration: content
hash, byte length, kind, media type, and the schema measured from
the bytes. The service rebuilds its trusted source catalog from
these records, so a reopened workspace keeps every imported
artifact without rereading or re-executing anything.

The `graph` kind and the graph identity map belong to
`melt/semantic-draft-1`; every other kind keeps its v0.1 shape.
ArtifactRecord.title: ArtifactRecord

CapturedParameter.description:
One parameter captured at admission (SPEC.md section 7.3).

``revision`` is the state revision of the captured value.
``incarnation`` is the identity incarnation of the parameter the
admission captured: deleting and recreating a parameter starts a
new incarnation while the state revision begins again at one
(SPEC.md section 12.3), so the revision alone cannot prove the
captured value still belongs to the same parameter.

A record saved before identity capture holds no incarnation. Such
a capture reads as the first incarnation, which no recreation can
satisfy again: a recreation only moves the stored incarnation
above one, so an older record stays publishable exactly while its
parameter was never recreated.
CapturedParameter.title: CapturedParameter

CommandReceipt.description:
The stored response of one processed request (section 12.5).

A retry with the same ID and payload returns the stored response.
Reuse with different content fails with `E_REQUEST_REUSE`.
CommandReceipt.title: CommandReceipt

Diagnostic.description: One diagnostic in the shape that SPEC.md section 11.3 defines.
Diagnostic.title: Diagnostic

Document.description:
The canonical document (SPEC.md section 4.1).

Every field is required. Collections may be empty. The document
holds definitions and current published source references only.
Document.title: Document

EventFieldValue.description: One value selector: a declared field of the event payload.
EventFieldValue.title: EventFieldValue

Filter.description:
One table filter.

`isNull` omits `value`. `contains` accepts only strings. Order
comparisons accept numbers, dates, timestamps, and strings. The
reader checks operators against column types (SPEC.md section
12.7).
Filter.title: Filter

GraphConfig.description: The renderer configuration of one graph projection.
GraphConfig.title: GraphConfig

GraphEdge.description: One edge between two existing nodes, by their node IDs.
GraphEdge.title: GraphEdge

GraphNode.description:
One node of the minimal graph contract (RFC 001 section 7.1).

`nodeId` identifies the visual element; the collection and key name
the semantic object it represents. Node IDs and object identities
stay separate: several nodes may carry the same reference.
GraphNode.title: GraphNode

GraphObservers.description: The observer slots of one graph projection.
GraphObservers.title: GraphObservers

GraphProjection.description:
One projection over an immutable graph source (RFC 001 6, 7.1).

The graph declares the one collection its nodes reference, so
selection has one static reference type. Nodes outside that
collection are rejected by validation.
GraphProjection.title: GraphProjection

GraphSchema.description:
The typed graph and its validated identity map (RFC 001 7.1).

The identity map is measured from the artifact bytes at import and
stored with the source version, so compilation never derives object
identity from labels or element order.
GraphSchema.title: GraphSchema

GraphSource.description: One logical graph source of immutable graph versions.
GraphSource.title: GraphSource

GraphSourceVersion.description: One version of a graph source: the measured identity map.
GraphSourceVersion.title: GraphSourceVersion

HighlightObserve.description: The `highlight` selector: which state the graph highlights by.
HighlightObserve.title: HighlightObserve

HostViewRecord.description: Service-owned native view settings, outside exported documents (section 10).
HostViewRecord.title: HostViewRecord

NullLiteralValue.description: One value selector: the typed null literal.
NullLiteralValue.title: NullLiteralValue

ObjectSelectEvent.description: One selection gesture: carries one semantic reference.
ObjectSelectEvent.title: ObjectSelectEvent

OutputGroupRecord.description:
The scheduling counters of one output group (sections 7.3, 13.3).

The service reserves a monotonically increasing `generation` for
every qualifying event of the group, in the same transaction that
admits an intent or commits the triggering user change. A generation
is never reused, and an older run stops being eligible for current
publication the moment a newer generation exists. `revision` is the
output group revision: it starts at 1 and increments when targets,
target kinds, output contracts, or ownership change.
OutputGroupRecord.title: OutputGroupRecord

OutputSubscription.description:
One projection source that follows an action output (RFC 001 8.1).

``follow: "current"`` resolves the output's current pointer at
every commit sequence, so the subscriber advances with each
successful publication. ``follow: "pinned"`` freezes one version of
the output's stable logical source: the subscriber does not
advance, and its view reports the version status it holds.
OutputSubscription.title: OutputSubscription

PageResponse.description:
One table page response (section 12.7).

`nextOffset` is null exactly at the end of the table. Rows are
arrays in the returned column order.
PageResponse.title: PageResponse

ParameterConstraints.description:
Constraints for every parameter type in one shape.

The semantic pass checks that only the fields of the declared type
are present, and that the default satisfies them.
ParameterConstraints.title: ParameterConstraints

ParameterContractEntry.description: One parameter slot in a registration contract.
ParameterContractEntry.title: ParameterContractEntry

ParameterState.description:
The stored value and revision of one parameter (section 6.2).

Revisions begin at 1. A successful value change increments the
revision.
ParameterState.title: ParameterState

PendingIntentRecord.description:
One pending request of an output group (sections 9.3 and 13.1).

The service owns the debounce timers, so the newest pending intent
of each output group is persisted with its captured invocation
snapshot and its due time. A repeated event replaces this record and
restarts its timer; a restart marks it interrupted instead of
executing it. The captured values are immutable from the moment they
are captured: the dispatched run receives exactly them.

``outputIncarnation`` is the stable output identity of the owning
action the intent captured (RFC 001 section 8.1). The dispatched
run carries it forward, so the current pointer of an output stays
bound to the calculation that published it even when another action
later reuses the group name.
PendingIntentRecord.title: PendingIntentRecord

PermissionGrantRecord.description:
One execution grant held outside every exported document (15.1).

A document never carries a grant: grants live in the service record
stream, minted only through the authenticated host permission
endpoint, never through a command envelope. A `specificRun` grant
covers exactly one captured admission intent and pins the definition
revisions it approved, so a changed action, registration, or output
group stops it from covering and a new admission is required. A
`projectExecution` grant covers every admission of one trusted
registration under the explicit project trust policy the host
recorded. Revocation is durable and covers nothing afterwards.
PermissionGrantRecord.title: PermissionGrantRecord

PublicationRecord.description:
One publication receipt (SPEC.md sections 13.4 and 14).

The publication transaction stores this record beside the run record
it concluded: the run keeps its disposition and output references,
while this receipt names the attempt itself. Recovery reconciles
staging directories against these receipts (section 14, startup step
6): a staging tree whose run holds no receipt marks work whose
publication never committed.
PublicationRecord.title: PublicationRecord

RecordConfig.description:
The renderer configuration of one record projection.

`fields` is null for every column of the collection's pinned
version, or an ordered list of distinct column identifiers.
RecordConfig.title: RecordConfig

RecordObserve.description: The `record` selector: which state resolves the shown record.
RecordObserve.title: RecordObserve

RecordObservers.description: The observer slots of one record projection.
RecordObservers.title: RecordObservers

RecordProjection.description:
One projection that resolves a reference in one collection.

The record selector reads state and sources; it writes neither. A
null selection displays an empty state, a missing key displays the
missing key, and an unreadable source displays a recoverable error
(RFC 001 section 6).
RecordProjection.title: RecordProjection

ReferenceState.description:
The stored value and revision of one reference state entry
(RFC 001 section 4).

The value is one serialized semantic reference or null. Revisions
begin at 1 and a successful assignment increments them, exactly as
parameter state does. A reference that a newer source version
leaves unresolved stays stored: resolution is reported, never
rewritten (RFC 001 section 3.3).
ReferenceState.title: ReferenceState

ReferenceType.description:
The type of one reference state entry (RFC 001 section 4).

Only `ref` exists in this extension. Numeric and string parameters
keep their v0.1 shape and are not migrated into this state system.
ReferenceType.title: ReferenceType

RegistrationRecord.description:
A service-owned trusted registration (SPEC.md section 7.2).

Registration never executes the script. The replay classification
is fixed to `nonReplaySafe` for arbitrary Python.
RegistrationRecord.title: RegistrationRecord

RunRecord.description:
One admitted or completed run, with its invocation snapshot.

The snapshot is immutable from admission (SPEC.md section 7.3):
``parameters`` carries each mapped parameter's captured value,
state revision, and identity incarnation, and ``parameterIds``
names the workspace parameter each captured entry addressed, so
launch and publication compare identity without consulting a
definition that may since have changed. A record saved before
identity capture holds no map and captures without incarnations;
both read through their defaults (:class:`CapturedParameter`).

``outputIncarnation`` is the stable output identity of the owning
action the run captured (RFC 001 section 8.1). The publication
group name is reusable, so it cannot identify a calculation: a
run belongs to the action that admitted it, and the incarnation
proves that action was never deleted and recreated. A record
saved before output identity capture holds none; such a run
resolves through its owning action alone, exactly as it did
before the field existed, and the same-transaction invalidation
of a recreation still retires it.
RunRecord.title: RunRecord

SelectionClearEvent.description: One clearing gesture: carries no object data.
SelectionClearEvent.title: SelectionClearEvent

SemanticAction.description:
One action of `melt/semantic-draft-1` (RFC 001 section 8.1).

The extension action declares output names, kinds, and a
publication group. It carries no projection targets: publication is
independent of panes, and projections subscribe to an output by its
stable incarnation instead. An action with no subscribers can still
run and publish, and closing, hiding, or removing a projection
neither cancels it nor invalidates its outputs.
SemanticAction.title: SemanticAction

SemanticBinding.description:
One binding of `melt/semantic-draft-1`.

A pure renderer event commits immediately: its debounce is fixed at
zero, because the service checks the event and commits the state
change and receipt together (RFC 001 section 5.3).
SemanticBinding.title: SemanticBinding

SemanticCollection.description:
One typed identity index over a table source (RFC 001 section 3.1).

`source` pins one immutable source version; updating it is a
revision-checked mutation. `key` names the column whose values are
the object keys: unique, non-null strings, compared case-sensitively
and never trimmed or normalized.
SemanticCollection.title: SemanticCollection

SemanticDocument.description:
The `melt/semantic-draft-1` document.

Every v0.1 field keeps its v0.1 meaning and checks. The two added
maps are required, like every other top-level collection, and may
be empty. The graph and record projections and the pure-event
bindings extend their v0.1 counterparts without changing them, and
the actions of this language declare outputs without projection
targets (RFC 001 section 8.1).
SemanticDocument.title: SemanticDocument

SemanticReference.description:
One serialized semantic reference (RFC 001 section 3.2).

References are workspace-scoped and carry no source version:
resolution uses the collection's current pinned version, and run
inputs capture their versions separately.
SemanticReference.title: SemanticReference

SemanticState.description:
One nullable reference state entry with workspace scope.

The default is null and only null: a reference value carries the
service-issued incarnation of its collection, so no document can
name one before the service creates the collection. Defaults apply
only on creation; changing one never resets a selection.
SemanticState.title: SemanticState

Snapshot.description:
A full workspace snapshot (section 12.4).

The snapshot separates the document from runtime records: entity
revisions, parameter state, and active runs. The service commits one
snapshot with every successful mutation, so reopening a workspace
restores the last committed definitions and state without executing
project code (SPEC.md section 14).

`incarnations` counts how often each parameter identifier was
created. Deleting and recreating a parameter starts a new identity
incarnation, so old events cannot target the new one (section 12.3).

`collectionIncarnations` and `referenceStates` carry the RFC 001
extension state of `melt/semantic-draft-1` workspaces: the opaque
incarnation the service issued for each semantic collection, and
the stored reference value and revision of each state entry.
`outputIncarnations` carries the stable output incarnation the
service issued for each action of the extension (RFC 001 8.1).
All three stay empty for a `melt/v0.1` workspace, whose snapshots
are unchanged.
Snapshot.title: Snapshot

SourceReference.description: A source reference is exactly a source ID and a version.
SourceReference.title: SourceReference

StateSetEffect.description:
One typed assignment: this binding writes one state record.

The value selector names a declared event field or a typed literal.
There are no expressions, function calls, string interpolations, or
executable callbacks (RFC 001 section 5.2).
StateSetEffect.title: StateSetEffect
